## Round 1: The Offline Pen and Paper Gauntlet

The first round was a classic offline test, designed to filter candidates based on their fundamental knowledge. We were given one hour to solve 20 questions, split into two sections.

### Section 1: C Programming (10 Questions)

This section was the tougher of the two, with a difficulty level ranging from moderate to hard. It was a true test of your ability to trace code and understand core C concepts. The questions were primarily focused on:

* **Output Prediction:** The majority of the questions involved complex nested loops, requiring you to manually iterate up to 100 times to predict the final output. This tested patience and precision.
* **Pointers & Recursion:** There was one dedicated question on pointers and another on recursion, diving into how memory and call stacks behave.
* **Macros:** A tricky question on macros tested understanding of pre-processor directives and their pitfalls.

My advice for this section is to have an extremely strong command of C fundamentals. Don’t just know the theory; practice dry-running complex code snippets by hand.

### Section 2: Quantitative Aptitude (10 Questions)

This part was a more standard aptitude test, with a difficulty level of easy to moderate. The topics covered were:

* Speed, Distance, and Time
* Work and Time
* Problems on Ages and Clocks
* Area and Percentages

With a good foundation from general aptitude preparation, this section is very manageable. The key is speed and accuracy to save as much time as possible for the challenging C questions.
